JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 1
SYSTEM MODELING ACTIVITY
JAPZ ERP: JAPZ Grill Burger & Bistro
Restaurant Inventory System
Inventory Management Module | 17 Required Diagrams
Project identification
The inventory module manages supplies, suppliers, receiving, batches, counts, waste, returns
and movement history. It also supports recipes, prepared stock and inventory reports through a
React interface, Express services and a MySQL database. Inventory Staff handle daily stock
work; Admin controls count approvals, reversals and policy settings.
Structural blueprinting
The System Architecture Diagram identifies the presentation, application and data boundaries
that developers must connect. It refines the supplied first version using the actual
React/TypeScript/Vite, Node.js/Express, Sequelize and MySQL implementation.
Behavioral blueprinting
The Use Case Diagram defines inventory goals and role permissions. The Activity Diagram
maps stock receiving, including duplicate-request checks, unit conversion, atomic updates and
rollback on failure.
Data blueprinting
Staff submit delivery lines and a unique request ID. The backend checks access, begins a
transaction, checks request identity, validates input and converts quantities to g, ml or pcs.
Receipt, line, batch, balance, movement and result changes commit together. Errors roll back;
identical retries return the saved result.
Scope and evidence
Current code is the primary evidence, and other modules appear only at inventory boundaries.
Examples, modeling abstractions and deployment or timing limitations are identified beside the
relevant diagrams.
Prepared 13 October 2026. No application source or business records were changed.

Page 3
01. System Architecture Diagram
This left-to-right view follows the web client through the guarded inventory API to peer handler/service groups and shared Sequelize persistence. The MySQL boundary distinguishes inventory records from user, menu and
order references shared with the application.
Implementation note: Reports and movement history run in inventory route handlers. Handler/service groups share Sequelize models within one Express backend.

backend/services/menuAvailability.js; japz-backend/services/inventorySettings.js; japz-backend/models/inventoryModels.js; japz-backend/models/menuItemModel.js; japz-backend/models/db.js

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 4
02. Class Diagram
This class diagram shows the receiving model relationships and the supporting inventory classes, with selected attributes and actual service functions. Stock quantities use decimals for supplies and integers for prepared menu
stock.
Implementation note: Multiplicity is shown on the principal associations; supporting references remain typed attributes to preserve readability. StockCount/WasteReport link to StockItem and StockBatch; MenuRecipe links to MenuItem;
StockAllocation links to Order. User audit references are shown without expanding user management. Service functions are module operations, not invented model methods.
Source: japz-backend/models/inventoryModels.js; japz-backend/models/index.js; japz-backend/models/menuItemModel.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 5
03. Component Diagram
Inventory screens use the data provider and HTTP client to call the inventory router. The router depends on access checks, inventory services and model queries; the access middleware loads the shared User model.
Implementation note: These logical components run within one frontend and one backend. Reporting queries execute in route handlers; no separate reporting service or API gateway is implemented.
Source: japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js; japz-web/src/features/inventory/Receiving.tsx; japz-backend/middleware/access.js; japz-web/src/features/inventory/InventoryData.tsx

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 6
04. Deployment Diagram
The deployment diagram places the inventory UI, backend code and database schema in their configured browser, Node.js and MySQL execution environments on the local workstation. Communication paths identify
HTTP/JSON requests and the MySQL protocol.
Implementation note: Configured development ports are Vite 5173, Express 3000 and MySQL 3306. render.yaml supplies backend hosting configuration, but no live cloud topology, load balancer or backup service is verified.
Source: start-local.ps1; japz-backend/index.js; japz-backend/models/db.js; japz-web/package.json; render.yaml

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 7
05. Object Diagram
This object diagram instantiates the receiving classes after one example receipt. Underlined instance names, attribute slots and solid links show a consistent snapshot of supplier, item, batch, receipt, line and movement
objects.
Implementation note: All IDs, names, dates and values are illustrative. They describe a valid implemented operation and do not claim these records exist in the business database.
Source: japz-backend/models/inventoryModels.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js:390

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 8
06. Package Diagram
Frontend inventory screens depend on shared HTTP, authentication and request-ID utilities. Backend routes use inventory services and models, including direct report/history queries; services use the persistence models.
Implementation note: Grouped utility directories and route/middleware directories are logical package groupings, not new physical folders or independently deployed services.
Source: japz-web/src/features/inventory; japz-web/src/services/api.ts; japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/services; japz-backend/models

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 9
07. Composite Structure Diagram
The composite structure diagram opens the inventory router boundary to show its collaborating middleware, route handler, stock service and Sequelize model parts. Ports represent the HTTP request boundary and SQL
persistence boundary.
Implementation note: The implementation uses modules, functions and an Express Router object. This UML structured classifier is a documentation abstraction, not an additional runtime inventory class.
Source: japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/middleware/access.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 10
08. Profile Diagram
JAPZInventoryProfile defines domain-specific stereotypes for inventory records, service components and stock operations. Each definition carries a tagged value and extends its corresponding UML metaclass.
Implementation note: This is a proposed documentation profile required by the activity. The application has no implemented UML profile loader or formal modeling-tool integration.
Source: japz-backend/models/inventoryModels.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js; OMG UML 2.5.1, Profiles

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 11
09. Data Flow Diagram (DFD)
This level 1 DFD follows stock receiving data from an authorized actor through authentication, receipt processing and presentation. It includes user records, duplicate-request records and the stock persistence data store.
Implementation note: D3 groups actual inventory tables, including suppliers; it is not a new database table. The browser subsequently reads updated balances. DFD arrows carry data and do not imply transaction control order.
Source: japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/middleware/access.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js; japz-web/src/features/inventory/Receiving.tsx

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 12
10. Use Case Diagram
Inventory Staff and Admin share the inventory operating goals shown on the left; the Admin actor also performs count review, reversals and policy control. Cashier and Kitchen appear at inventory read boundaries, and Kitchen
can submit and view its own waste reports.
Implementation note: Inventory Operator is a diagram actor grouping, not an extra application role. Authentication and approved user status are preconditions. Inventory screens require Inventory/Admin; the boundary actors use their
permitted API interactions.
Source: japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/services/inventorySettings.js; japz-web/src/App.tsx

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 13
11. Activity Diagram
This activity models receiving access checks, request identity branches and the transaction that creates receipt records and stock changes. A new successful request commits; an identical retry returns its prior result;
conflicting identities and write errors abort the attempt.
Implementation note: The outcome decision summarizes exceptions across the enclosed write sequence. Corrections begin a new submission; a failed operation does not leave partially committed inventory changes.
Source: japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js; japz-web/src/features/inventory/Receiving.tsx

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 14
12. Sequence Diagram
The sequence follows one new receiving request through the browser, inventory API and persistence boundary. The loop fragment represents the actual per-line validation, conversion and stock writes before the operation
result and receipt commit together.
Implementation note: Router and services share an API lifeline; Sequelize and MySQL share a persistence lifeline. Alternatives are summarized in the note and expanded as activity branches in Diagram 11.
Source: japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js; japz-web/src/features/inventory/Receiving.tsx; japz-backend/middleware/access.js

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 15
13. State Machine Diagram
StockCount records begin as pending when review is required, or applied when the actor and policy permit immediate adjustment. Admin approval applies only if the item version still matches and counted stock protects
reservations; otherwise the record becomes stale. Rejection leaves balances unchanged.
Implementation note: Choice diamonds are UML pseudostates, not additional database status values. Invalid input is rejected before creation. Review policy depends on role, countApproval and the item adjustmentLimit.
Source: japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js; japz-backend/models/inventoryModels.js

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 16
14. Communication Diagram
This communication diagram shows the actor, receiving UI, inventory API and persistence objects collaborating on a stock receipt. Nested message numbers describe authorization, transaction identity handling, repeated line
writes and commit along the API-to-persistence link.
Implementation note: The inventory API groups existing middleware, route handlers and services for readability; it is not an added runtime class. Return messages are dashed, and repeated line messages use the UML iteration marker.
Source: japz-backend/routes/inventory.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js; japz-web/src/features/inventory/Receiving.tsx

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 17
15. Interaction Overview Diagram
The interaction overview connects receiving authorization, the detailed stock transaction and inventory readback as referenced interactions. Decisions route denied access and failed transactions to their corresponding UI
outcomes.
Implementation note: The stock transaction interaction is expanded in Diagram 12. Failure paths end the current attempt; a corrected submission begins a new interaction. No parallel background save is implied.
Source: japz-backend/middleware/access.js; japz-backend/services/inventoryService.js; japz-web/src/features/inventory/Receiving.tsx; japz-web/src/features/inventory/InventoryData.tsx

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 18
16. Timing Diagram
This timing diagram shows the visible-tab state and refresh/request states across the configured 30-second polling ticks. The initial refresh and subsequent successful requests update the inventory data and timestamp.
Implementation note: The illustrated 3- and 4-second request durations are examples only. setInterval is a schedule, not a deadline guarantee; hidden tabs skip interval-triggered requests, focus/manual refresh can run earlier, and older
responses are ignored using a sequence counter. No real-time push or hard latency guarantee is implemented.
Source: japz-web/src/features/inventory/InventoryData.tsx; japz-web/src/services/api.ts; japz-backend/services/inventorySettings.js

JAPZ ERP | Inventory Management
Page 19
17. Requirement Diagram (SysML)
The requirement diagram expresses five concrete inventory rules supported by the implementation and links each rule to the code element that satisfies it. SysML requirement blocks carry an ID and requirement text; satisfy
arrows point to the requirement.
Implementation note: These are implementation-derived documentation requirements. No independent client requirement baseline, formal SysML model or real-time performance requirement was supplied. Test code was inspected for
corresponding scenarios; this document does not claim a fresh test execution.
